### 7.1.4 Doctrinal Construction of Law and the Reconstruction of Individual Sovereignty

Facing this existential reality, traditional civil and public law doctrines must undergo a radical reconstruction (Hildebrandt, 2015). Within the Indonesian positive civil law system, for instance, the validity of an agreement is strictly governed by Article 1320 of the Indonesian Civil Code (*Burgerlijk Wetboek*), which stipulates that mutual consent of the parties bound is a prerequisite for validity. Article 1321 of the Indonesian Civil Code, read in conjunction with the doctrine of defects of will (*wilsgebreke*), recognizes classic concepts such as mistake (*dwaling*), duress (*dwang*), fraud (*bedrog*), and undue influence (*misbruik van omstandigheden*), all of which can render a legal engagement voidable (Subekti, 2005). The paramount challenge in the era of cognitive sovereignty lies in adapting these classical doctrines to a landscape where undue influence is no longer executed by humans face-to-face, but is instead systematically programmed into opaque, autonomous predictive algorithmic codes (Calo, 2014).

Globally, progressive steps have been taken through the enactment of the EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689)—specifically Article 5, which explicitly prohibits artificial intelligence practices that deploy subliminal techniques beyond a person's consciousness to materially distort their behavior in a manner that causes or is likely to cause physical or psychological harm (EU AI Act, 2024). Furthermore, Article 50 of the same regulation mandates strict transparency for AI-generated content, ensuring that individuals are not manipulated under conditions of ignorance. Conversely, personal data protection instruments such as the Indonesian Personal Data Protection Act (Law No. 27/2022) must be granted an expansive interpretation (Indonesian Personal Data Protection Act, 2022). Data protection cannot stop at the administrative facets of personal information; rather, it must encompass the safeguarding of cognitive derivations, psychological profiles, and neural biometric data extracted therefrom (Farahany, 2023).

This novel doctrinal construction necessitates the emergence of a new legal school of thought: Neuro-Cognitive Jurisprudence (Floridi, 2013). Within this framework, the burden of proof must be reversed (*reversed burden of proof*) (Calo, 2014). When a technology platform or AI system is accused of manipulating consciousness or exploiting users' mental vulnerabilities, the developing corporation must prove that its system architecture was designed with the highest standard of care (*duty of care*) to preserve the subject's cognitive autonomy, rather than optimizing for addiction and rational disorientation (Jonas, 1979). Manipulative design can no longer be viewed as a legitimate exercise of freedom of contract under Article 1338 of the Indonesian Civil Code; instead, it must be classified as an unlawful act (*onrechtmatige daad*) pursuant to Article 1365 of the Indonesian Civil Code, which breaches the boundaries of public order and universal morality (Subekti, 2005).

Ultimately, the reconstruction of individual sovereignty in the 21st century demands the recognition that the integrity of the mind is a non-derogable right under any circumstances (Universal Declaration of Human Rights, 1948; Farahany, 2023). States and corporations must be barred from turning human consciousness into a commodity that can be mined, manipulated, and traded in the free market of data (Zuboff, 2019). By establishing cognitive sovereignty as a new constitutional pillar, we not only rescue individual privacy from the clutches of predatory algorithms, but we also defend the very essence of humanity against the threat of moral extinction in the digital age (Weizenbaum, 1976; Wiener, 1950).

$$ \mathcal{C}_{lib} = \oint_{\partial \Omega} \left( \mathcal{I}_{mental} - \mathcal{M}_{alg} \right) d\sigma \geq \text{Threshold}_{Autonomy} $$

The mathematical formulation above depicts the minimum threshold of cognitive sovereignty equilibrium ($\mathcal{C}_{lib}$), where innate mental integrity ($\mathcal{I}_{mental}$) minus the intensity of external algorithmic manipulation ($\mathcal{M}_{alg}$) along the boundary of the subject's sphere of consciousness ($\partial \Omega$) must not fall below the minimum human autonomy threshold ($\text{Threshold}_{Autonomy}$) (Floridi, 2013; Turing, 1950). If this equation is violated by corporate or state power, the legal system is obligated to intervene correctively to restore substantive justice for humankind (Calo, 2014; EU AI Act, 2024).
